text_prompt: In the PLAX view, no aortic stenosis shows normal thin aortic valve leaflets with full systolic opening and no thickening, calcification, or turbulence.
In the PLAX view, early aortic stenosis shows mild thickening of the aortic valve leaflets with nearly normal opening and no obvious doming or turbulence.

In the PLAX view, significant aortic stenosis shows thickened, calcified, and immobile aortic valve leaflets with restricted systolic opening, left ventricular hypertrophy, and turbulent high-velocity flow.
In the PSAX view, no aortic stenosis shows normal thin aortic valve cusps with complete and regular systolic opening.
In the PSAX view, early aortic stenosis shows mild thickening of the aortic valve cusps with almost normal opening area.
In the PSAX view, severe aortic stenosis shows thickened, calcified, and poorly mobile aortic valve cusps with reduced and irregular systolic opening area.
No abnormal features related to aortic stenosis are observed in other ultrasound views.
No specific abnormal features of early aortic stenosis are observed in other ultrasound views.
In other cardiac ultrasound views besides PLAX and PSAX, significant aortic stenosis shows no additional specific visual features.
